citation.title: Effects of vitamin C, vitamin E, zinc gluconate, and selenomethionine supplementation on muscle function and oxidative stress biomarkers in patients with facioscapulohumeral dystrophy: a double-blind randomized controlled clinical trial

conclusion: Credible chronic inherited-muscle-disease functional-compensation challenger: randomized placebo-controlled quadriceps MVC and relative-load endurance gains for the exact four-component study combination. The walking endpoint used to power the study was nonsignificant. No individual-ingredient, BUBR1-restoration, MVA-efficacy or nominee-superiority claim.

preparation.source_label: Vitamin C, dl-alpha tocopheryl-acetate, zinc gluconate and selenomethionine combination
preparation.form: Separate encapsulated components, 120 capsules per bottle; manufacturer responsible for batch quality control according to main. No independent lot/COA verification.

active_as_reported.vitamin_C: 500 mg/day; main does not identify a precise stereochemical/formulation equivalent to the existing L-ascorbic-acid entry
active_as_reported.vitamin_E: 400 mg/day dl-alpha tocopheryl-acetate in Randomization and masking; more general alpha-tocopherol wording elsewhere
active_as_reported.zinc: 25 mg/day zinc gluconate explicitly stated to provide 3.5 mg elemental zinc in main
active_as_reported.selenium: 200 micrograms/day selenomethionine in main/abstract; current registry says selenium 200 micrograms/day in the form of selenomethionine. Compound-versus-element amount remains unresolved; no conversion asserted.

preparation.placebo: Matching microcrystalline-cellulose capsules, same manufacturer, reportedly indistinguishable
preparation.timing: Reported study schedule separates vitamin C at breakfast, zinc 1 hour later, selenium 3 hours later and vitamin E after dinner, with food. Recorded exposure description only, not a regimen recommendation.
preparation.product_equivalence: No generic supplement, ordinary food, retail product or isolated component inherits the mixture result.

alias_proposal.proposed_sole_preparation_scoped_alias: vitamin C, dl-alpha tocopheryl-acetate, zinc gluconate and selenomethionine combination
alias_proposal.basis: Each component/form is explicit in the same source Randomization and masking section; descriptive combination phrase, not a source-reported commercial brand.

design.population: Adults 18–60 years with 4–9 D4Z4 repeats and positive FSHD family history; wheelchair confinement, smoking, associated comorbidity and medication/supplement use excluded.
design.randomization: Computer-generated permuted blocks of 4, stratified on baseline dominant-quadriceps MVC at 5 kg; sealed allocation envelopes held by pharmacist. Extraction renders inequality symbols poorly; exact greater-than/less-than-or-equal distinction inferred from surrounding strata descriptions and is not a native-symbol check.
design.blinding: Participants and all personnel reportedly masked until completion; matching capsules.
design.duration: 17-week supplementation described; visits V1 baseline, V2 week 1 randomization, V3 week 17 function, V4 week 18 end/biomarkers. Main explicitly places functional testing after 16 weeks of exposure despite broader 17-week outcome wording.
design.cointerventions: No additional exercise-training intervention described; usual diet/activity control not sufficiently detailed to assume standardization.
design.baseline_imbalance: BMI higher in active arm; steppage gait 13/26 active versus 6/27 placebo. Source also discusses heterogeneous and imbalanced baseline force/endurance despite stratification.

hierarchy_registration.article: Abstract/Study outcomes list walking plus bilateral MVC/endurance as primary outcomes. Power calculation and Discussion single out 2-minute walk as the primary powering endpoint.
hierarchy_registration.power: Based on expected 30 m walking difference and prior SD 42 m; 25 per arm before 5% dropout allowance, one-sided alpha 5%, 80% power.
hierarchy_registration.current_registry: One broad primary muscle-effort-tolerance outcome includes 2MWT and/or MVC and/or quadriceps endurance; no precise statistical hierarchy confirmed.
hierarchy_registration.registration_interpretation: Retrospective relative to trial start and recorded primary completion; not evidence of prospective prespecification. Historical initial registry version and full protocol/SAP were not accessed.
hierarchy_registration.enrollment_difference: Registry 54 actual versus article 53 randomized; article 54 eligible before one exclusion plausibly accounts for difference but is not an independently verified registry explanation.
hierarchy_registration.date_consistency: Current registry primary completion February 2012 precedes the paper’s stated recruitment end April 2012; this inconsistency was not resolved from a historical registry version.

functional_results.direction: No statistically significant direct treatment contrast

endpoint_measurement.MVC: Seated strain-gauge force, reported in kg, knees/hips 90 degrees; best of 3–5 trials with at least two measurements within 10%. Absolute measured output, not mass-normalized torque.
endpoint_measurement.endurance: Repeated knee extension against 30% MVC at 10 movements/minute to exhaustion; dominant leg defined by stronger MVC. Main does not explicitly resolve whether follow-up resistance was held at baseline load or recalibrated. This is relative-load test performance, not demonstrated improvement at a common absolute workload.
endpoint_measurement.walking: Best of two 2-minute maximum-pace corridor walks separated by 20 minutes.

analysis_and_missingness.method: Linear mixed model for repeated measures; time, group and group×time fixed effects. Reported functional P values test group×time, not merely within-arm gains. General significance threshold P < .05; tail choice for outcome-model tests not explicitly stated.
analysis_and_missingness.multiplicity: No correction or hierarchical testing described across five functional tests and numerous secondary/correlation analyses; treat reported P values as nominal.
analysis_and_missingness.analysis_label: Authors call analyses intention-to-treat, but Tables 2–4 show 25 active/27 placebo before further endpoint limitations, not all 53 randomized.
analysis_and_missingness.main_active_gap: Reason for 26 randomized to 25 in main tables unresolved because native Figure 1 flow pixels unavailable; do not invent withdrawal reason or imputation.
analysis_and_missingness.endpoint_missingness: Inability to hold 3 second isometric contraction or perform 30% MVC/10 per minute endurance excluded measurements; endurance n 19/17 dominant and 18/16 nondominant, likely limiting applicability to more impaired patients.
analysis_and_missingness.reported_CIs: No functional treatment-effect CIs in accessible main.
analysis_and_missingness.raw_data_analysis: None. Only labelled arithmetic differences of rounded reported changes.
analysis_and_missingness.walking_subgroup: Without steppage gait, walking remained nonsignificant P = .157 in 34/53 reported patients; no rescue of overall null.
analysis_and_missingness.women_subgroup: Paper reports nonsignificant within-group change in women and calls further analysis in preparation; no sex-by-treatment interaction established.

biomarkers_and_mechanism: Selected direct vitamin C/E and lipid-peroxide changes accompany function; several other oxidative markers improve only within active arm or remain between-group nonpositive. Correlations do not establish antioxidant mediation, individual-component necessity or BUBR1/chromosome-fidelity restoration.

harms_and_support.reported_harms: Main says side effects were neither observed nor reported. No detailed AE table/severity taxonomy or long-term safety comparison in accessible text; do not translate this into proven safety.
harms_and_support.adherence: Among completers, 96% active and 100% placebo reported.
harms_and_support.funding: Stichting FSHD, Amis FSH Europe and Montpellier University Hospital (AOI).
harms_and_support.manufacturer_role: CRID PHARMA supplied active/placebo and handled product quality control.

publication_status.PubMed: Retained official record has journal-article/RCT labels and no CommentsCorrections link to correction/retraction.
publication_status.Crossref: Current DOI response contains no update-to/updated-by relation or correction/retraction notice.
publication_status.targeted_search: Exact DOI plus retraction/correction/erratum search did not expose a matching notice.
publication_status.limit: No notice found in this bounded check; not an exhaustive guarantee. Direct publisher XML contains metadata only, despite full-text-retrieval-response wrapper.

cohort_credit.companion: PMID26461290/DOI10.1016/j.freeradbiomed.2014.10.587 was exposed as a same-investigator conference report about the intervention; independent cohort status was not established, and no extra replication credit is assigned.

transfer_and_competitiveness: A real controlled chronic strength/endurance comparison in inherited muscular dystrophy is more causally informative for those functions than niacin’s uncontrolled human observation. It is not a head-to-head comparison with either nomination, not proven pediatric or MVA transfer, and cannot establish superiority to apitegromab in SMA. Apply the same functional-evidence standard; preserve gains and all stated scope limits.

baseline_source_references.resolution: Read this immutable Git blob for source/proposal verification; do not bind the future mutable live ledger as an eternal input.

integration_metadata.reading_roles: Source author and independent reviewer read the accessible author scientific main and extracted tables/captions with native-output limits. This proposal preserves their recorded depths; it assigns no additional source-reading credit to the integrating reviewer.
